quests.title: Your First Bucket
quests.intro: Every fish in my lake is an object and every net is a bucket. Let's put the city's brochure in a bucket and send it around the world.

steps.text: Walk to S3 Lake and talk to Sally
Learn 5 S3 cards, like buckets, durability and storage classes
Learn 3 CloudFront cards about keeping copies near people (edge caching)
Design the City Brochure Site with S3, CloudFront and Route 53
Build it for real: a private S3 bucket served by CloudFront

quests.title: Fire Up the Grill
quests.intro: Welcome to the Compute Quarter! I only light the grill when an order comes in, so let me show you how serverless functions answer the city's requests.

steps.text: Walk to the Lambda Food Stall and say hello
Learn 5 Lambda cards, like pricing, timeouts and memory
Build the Thumbnail Factory: resize every uploaded photo automatically

steps.prompt: What is a cold start in AWS Lambda and how can I reduce it?
steps.text: Ask the agents about cold starts
Build your first web API with Cody, with no servers to run (serverless)

quests.title: The Librarian's Card Index
quests.intro: Tell me the exact card number and I'll fetch it in milliseconds. Let me teach you how to pick keys, and how to keep the library open on two continents.

steps.text: Walk to the DynamoDB Library and meet the librarian
Learn 5 DynamoDB cards, like keys, capacity modes and indexes
Learn 3 Aurora cards at the Observatory
Keep the booking system running across two Regions
Build a pay-per-request DynamoDB table with backups (point-in-time recovery)

quests.title: Market Day Rush
quests.intro: Letters wait patiently in my queue until someone is ready. On market day that patience is what stops the bakery from losing orders!

steps.text: Walk to the Queue & Bell Tower and talk to Quinn
Learn 5 SQS & SNS cards, like queues, timeouts and dead-letter queues
Learn 3 API Gateway cards at the station
Design an order pipeline that never drops an order

steps.prompt: When should I use SQS, SNS or EventBridge?
steps.text: Ask the agents to compare the three messengers
Build a queue with a Lambda worker and a dead-letter queue for failures

quests.title: The Night Watch
quests.intro: Nobody passes my gate without a badge. Together we'll lock down identities, then set a watch that never sleeps and a wall that holds against the storm.

steps.text: Walk to the IAM Gatehouse and talk to Ivy
Learn 5 IAM cards, like roles, least privilege and explicit deny
Learn 3 GuardDuty cards at the Watchtower
Detect threats and respond automatically, even at 3 a.m.
Keep the ticket shop open in a flood of junk traffic (DDoS)

steps.prompt: What is the difference between CloudWatch and CloudTrail?
steps.text: Ask the agents: watching versus record-keeping (monitoring vs auditing)

quests.title: Ask Bedrock
quests.intro: Ask me anything, traveller. One service reaches many foundation models, and with a Knowledge Base my answers come from your own documents.

steps.text: Walk to the Bedrock Mesa
Learn 5 Bedrock cards, like tokens and looking things up first (RAG)

steps.prompt: Explain retrieval-augmented generation in two sentences, with an AWS example.
steps.text: Ask the agents what RAG means
Help a staff helper answer from the city's handbook, then meet AgentCore

quests.title: Build an AI Agent
quests.intro: At the Academy every agent gets a runtime, a memory, tools and an identity. Let's enrol your first one and make sure it behaves.

steps.text: Walk to the AgentCore Academy and meet Ace
Learn all 8 AgentCore cards, like Runtime, Memory, Gateway and Identity
Learn 3 Cognito cards so your agent knows who it serves
Build the Staff Helper agent

steps.prompt: How does AgentCore Gateway turn a Lambda function into a tool my agent can call?
steps.text: Ask the agents how agents get tools

quests.title: Your First Data Lake
quests.intro: I crawl the lake and label every shelf. Once the catalogue is written, Athena can shine her SQL beam right across the water.

steps.text: Walk to the Glue Workshop and talk to Gus
Learn 4 Glue cards, like the Data Catalog, crawlers and pricing
Learn 4 Athena cards, like SQL on S3 and pay-per-scan
Visit the Lake Formation Gate to see who may read what
Search the Lake of Receipts while hiding private columns

steps.prompt: Why does converting CSV to partitioned Parquet make Athena cheaper?
steps.text: Ask the agents how to cut query costs

quests.title: Ship It in Containers
quests.intro: Every box on my ships is a container: the app and everything it needs, packed once and run anywhere. Let's ship the harbour shop without patching a single server.

steps.text: Walk to the ECS Shipping Docks and meet Captain Cass
Learn 4 ECS cards, like tasks, services and roles
Learn 3 Fargate cards about running containers with no servers to manage
Design the Harbour Container Shop

steps.prompt: When should I run containers on AWS Fargate instead of on EC2 instances I manage?
steps.text: Ask the agents: Fargate or EC2 for containers?

quests.title: Walls, Gates and Keys
quests.intro: My garden has walls, gates and guards, and Kit's vault keeps the keys. Learn how a network keeps traffic out, then build a members-only API where sign-in, not walls, decides who gets in.

steps.text: Walk to the VPC Walled Garden and meet Vic
Learn 4 VPC cards, like subnets, gateways and security groups
Visit Kit at the KMS Vault
Learn 3 KMS cards about keys and encryption
Design the Members-Only API (no VPC needed)

steps.prompt: What is the difference between a security group and a network ACL in a VPC?
steps.text: Ask the agents how a VPC keeps traffic out

quests.title: The Machine Shop
quests.intro: Every machine on my factory floor is rented by the second. Pick the right size and the right deal, and you never pay for idle steel.

steps.text: Walk to the EC2 Factory and meet Eddie
Learn 5 EC2 cards, like instance types, AMIs and pricing options
Help a website survive its Friday rush
steps.question: A team's website runs on one EC2 server. Traffic doubles every Friday evening, then drops for the rest of the week. What keeps it fast without paying for big servers all week?

options.text: An Auto Scaling group that adds servers when it gets busy and removes them after
options.why: It scales out for the rush and back in afterwards, so you pay only for the servers that are running.

options.text: Buy the biggest instance size and leave it on all week
options.why: That pays for Friday-night capacity every hour of every day.

options.text: Turn on termination protection
options.why: That only stops someone deleting the server by mistake. It adds no capacity.

steps.text: Pick the cheapest way to run a batch job
steps.question: A nightly batch job can be stopped and restarted without harm. Which way of buying EC2 capacity costs the least?

options.text: Spot Instances
options.why: Spare EC2 capacity at a large discount. AWS can take it back with a two-minute warning, which an interruptible job can handle.

options.text: On-Demand Instances
options.why: Full price by the second, with no commitment. Right for work that must not be interrupted.

options.text: Dedicated Hosts
options.why: A whole physical server just for you: useful for some software licences, and the most expensive option here.

quests.title: Kube's Harbour
quests.intro: Kubernetes is the shipping system half the world already uses. I run its control tower for you; you bring the ships.

steps.text: Walk to the EKS Harbour Tower and meet Kube
Learn 4 EKS cards about clusters, pods and nodes
Find out what Kube runs for you
steps.question: When you create an Amazon EKS cluster, what does AWS run and look after for you?

options.text: The Kubernetes control plane, spread across several Availability Zones
options.why: AWS runs and patches the control plane. Your pods still run on nodes: EC2 servers, or AWS Fargate.

options.text: Your containers, with no nodes or capacity needed at all
options.why: Pods need somewhere to run: EC2 nodes, managed node groups or AWS Fargate.

options.text: A new image format that replaces your container images
options.why: You still build ordinary container images. EKS runs standard Kubernetes.

steps.text: Choose between two container harbours
steps.question: A team already runs Kubernetes in its own data centre and wants to keep the same tools and skills on AWS. Which service fits best?

options.text: Amazon EKS
options.why: It runs standard, upstream Kubernetes, so the team keeps its tools, manifests and know-how.

options.text: Amazon ECS
options.why: A simpler AWS container service, but it isn't Kubernetes: the team would learn a new way of working.

options.text: AWS Lambda
options.why: Functions that run on demand. Good for events, but not a place to run a Kubernetes setup.

quests.title: Plant It and Grow
quests.intro: Bring me your code and I'll grow everything around it: servers, a load balancer, scaling and health checks. You can still look under the leaves.

steps.text: Walk to Beanstalk Garden and meet Jack
Learn 4 Elastic Beanstalk cards about environments and deploys
Pick a home for a small web app
steps.question: A student has a small web app. They don't want to set up servers, load balancers and scaling by hand, but they want to see the servers that run it. Which service fits?

options.text: AWS Elastic Beanstalk
options.why: Upload the code and it creates the EC2 servers, load balancer and scaling for you, and you can still open every one of them.

options.text: Amazon Redshift
options.why: A data warehouse for analysing huge tables. It doesn't host web apps.

options.text: AWS KMS
options.why: It looks after encryption keys. It doesn't run code.

steps.text: Find out what Beanstalk itself costs
steps.question: What do you pay for Elastic Beanstalk itself?

options.text: Nothing extra: you pay only for the resources it creates, like EC2 servers and the load balancer
options.why: Beanstalk has no charge of its own. Turn the environment off and its servers stop costing money.

options.text: A monthly fee per app, on top of the servers
options.why: There's no extra fee for Beanstalk itself.

options.text: A charge for every deploy
options.why: Deploys are free; you pay for what runs.

quests.title: Bex's Lockers
quests.intro: Each locker sits in one Availability Zone and plugs into a server there. Fast and private, but remember where it lives.

steps.text: Walk to the EBS Lockers and meet Bex
Learn 4 EBS cards about volumes, types and snapshots
Move a locker to another zone
steps.question: An EBS volume is in us-east-1a. Can a server in us-east-1b attach it?

options.text: No. A volume attaches only to servers in its own Availability Zone; take a snapshot and create a new volume there
options.why: Volumes live in one zone. A snapshot can make a copy in any zone of the Region, or be copied to another Region.

options.text: Yes, any server in the same Region can attach it
options.why: Volumes are tied to one Availability Zone.

options.text: Only if the volume is encrypted
options.why: Encryption protects the data; it doesn't change where the volume can attach.

steps.text: Keep a locker safe from a bad day
steps.question: How do you protect an EBS volume's data in case its Availability Zone has a problem?

options.text: Take regular snapshots (Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager can automate them)
options.why: Snapshots are stored across the Region, so you can rebuild the volume in another zone. Copy them to another Region for even more safety.

options.text: Make the volume bigger
options.why: More space doesn't make a second copy anywhere.

options.text: Attach the volume to two servers
options.why: Even where that's possible, both servers are in the same zone, so it doesn't help if that zone fails.

quests.title: The Shared Well
quests.intro: One well, many buckets dipping in at once. Servers in every zone draw the same water from me.

steps.text: Walk to the EFS Shared Well and meet Effie
Learn 4 EFS cards about shared file systems and storage classes
Give ten servers the same files
steps.question: Ten web servers in different Availability Zones must read and write the same files at the same time. Which storage fits?

options.text: Amazon EFS
options.why: A shared file system that many servers mount at once, across Availability Zones.

options.text: Amazon EBS
options.why: A volume lives in one Availability Zone and usually belongs to one server.

options.text: The server's own instance store
options.why: Fast, but the data disappears when the server stops, and no other server can see it.

steps.text: Pay less for files nobody opens
steps.question: Most files in a file system haven't been opened for months. How do you pay less without deleting them?

options.text: Turn on lifecycle management so EFS moves them to the Infrequent Access or Archive storage class
options.why: EFS moves cold files to cheaper classes automatically and brings them back when they're opened.

options.text: Copy them to an EBS volume
options.why: That adds a second bill and loses the sharing.

options.text: Make the file system read-only
options.why: That stops changes but doesn't make storage cheaper.

quests.title: Ray's Records Hall
quests.intro: Rows and columns, kept tidy. I patch the engine, take the backups and keep a standby ready, so you can get on with your app.

steps.text: Walk to the RDS Records Hall and meet Ray
Learn 5 RDS cards about engines, backups and Multi-AZ
Keep the ledgers open if a building fails
steps.question: What does a Multi-AZ deployment do for an RDS database?

options.text: Keeps a standby copy in another Availability Zone and fails over to it automatically
options.why: If the main database or its zone fails, RDS switches to the standby, usually within a minute or two.

options.text: Copies data to another Region to make reads faster there
options.why: That's a cross-Region read replica, a different feature.

options.text: Makes every query run faster
options.why: The standby is for failover. It doesn't speed up queries.

steps.text: Help a database that reads all day
steps.question: An app reads far more than it writes, and the database is getting busy. What helps most?

options.text: Add read replicas and send the reads to them
options.why: Replicas take copies of the data and answer read queries, so the main database has more room for writes.

options.text: Turn off automated backups
options.why: That removes your safety net and barely helps performance.

options.text: Move the database to a smaller instance
options.why: Less capacity makes a busy database slower.

quests.title: Reggie's Big Questions
quests.intro: Billions of rows, stacked in columns. Ask me something big, like ten years of sales by month, and I'll answer before your tea cools.

steps.text: Walk to the Redshift Warehouse and meet Reggie
Learn 4 Redshift cards about warehouses and columns
Pick the right job for the warehouse
steps.question: Which job suits Amazon Redshift best?

options.text: Analysing billions of sales rows to find trends across years
options.why: That's analytics (OLAP): big scans over many rows, which is what a data warehouse is built for.

options.text: Saving each shopping-cart click within milliseconds
options.why: Lots of tiny, fast writes (OLTP) suit a database like DynamoDB.

options.text: Storing customers' profile photos
options.why: Files and photos belong in Amazon S3.

steps.text: Find out why columns are fast
steps.question: Why does Redshift store data by column rather than by row?

options.text: A question about a few columns reads only those columns, so big scans are faster and compress better
options.why: Values in a column are alike, so they compress well, and unused columns are never read.

options.text: So each row can be updated faster
options.why: Single-row updates are what row-based databases do best.

options.text: Because columns never need backups
options.why: Redshift still takes snapshots of your data.

quests.title: Nep's Web
quests.intro: Who knows whom, who bought what, what links to what: I keep the threads, so you can walk from one to the next.

steps.text: Walk to Neptune Web and meet Nep
Learn 4 Neptune cards about graphs, nodes and edges
Pick a question for a graph
steps.question: Which question is a graph database like Amazon Neptune best at?

options.text: Which friends of my friends bought this book?
options.why: Following links between people and things, hop after hop, is what graphs are made for.

options.text: What were our total sales last year?
options.why: A big sum over many rows is a job for a data warehouse like Redshift.

options.text: Where should I store this video file?
options.why: Files belong in Amazon S3.

steps.text: Learn how to ask Nep a question
steps.question: Which query languages can you use with Amazon Neptune?

options.text: Graph query languages such as Gremlin and openCypher
options.why: Neptune answers graph questions in graph languages (it also speaks one made for linked web data), not in SQL.

options.text: Only SQL
options.why: Neptune is a graph database; it speaks graph query languages, not SQL.

options.text: Spreadsheet formulas
options.why: Spreadsheets are for tables, not graphs.

quests.title: Sage's Workbench
quests.intro: Some models you borrow; some you build. In my workshop you bring the data, train the model and send it out to answer questions.

steps.text: Walk to the SageMaker Workshop and meet Sage
Learn 4 SageMaker AI cards about training and endpoints
Choose between building and borrowing a model
steps.question: When would you pick Amazon SageMaker AI over Amazon Bedrock?

options.text: When you want to train or tune your own model on your own data and control the training
options.why: SageMaker AI gives you the tools to build, train and deploy models yourself.

options.text: When you just want to call a ready-made foundation model through an API
options.why: That's Amazon Bedrock: no training or servers to manage.

options.text: When you need to store training files
options.why: Training data usually lives in Amazon S3, whichever service trains the model.

steps.text: Put a trained model to work
steps.question: A trained model must answer requests from your app all day. What do you create in SageMaker AI?

options.text: A real-time inference endpoint
options.why: An endpoint keeps the model loaded and answers each request as it arrives.

options.text: A training job
options.why: A training job builds the model, then stops. It doesn't answer requests.

options.text: A notebook
options.why: Notebooks are for exploring data and experimenting, not for serving an app.

quests.title: Ask Quill
quests.intro: Stuck on an error? Lost in the console? Ask me where you work. I'll explain, suggest and point you to the docs, and you stay in charge.

steps.text: Walk to the Q Help Desk and meet Quill
Learn 4 Amazon Q cards about asking for help where you work
Get help with a confusing error
steps.question: Your Lambda function fails in the AWS console with an error you don't understand. How can Amazon Q help?

options.text: Ask Amazon Q in the console to explain the error and suggest how to fix it
options.why: Amazon Q can help diagnose console errors and explain them in plain words, right where you are.

options.text: It quietly changes your resources to fix the error
options.why: Amazon Q explains and suggests; you decide what to change.

options.text: It deletes the function and starts again
options.why: That would lose your code. Q helps you understand the problem instead.

steps.text: Decide how much to trust an assistant
steps.question: Is everything an AI assistant like Amazon Q says always right?

options.text: No. Check its answers, as you would anyone's, before you change anything important
options.why: AI assistants can be wrong. Read the suggestion, check the docs it links, and test changes safely.

options.text: Yes, it can't make mistakes
options.why: Every AI assistant can make mistakes.

options.text: Only on weekends
options.why: Mistakes don't keep a calendar. Always check.

quests.title: Rex's Gallery
quests.intro: Every picture that comes through my doors gets a look: what's in it, whether it's safe, and whose face it might be in your own collection.

steps.text: Walk to the Rekognition Gallery and meet Rex
Learn 4 Rekognition cards about labels, faces and moderation
Keep unsafe pictures off an app
steps.question: A photo-sharing app must stop unsafe images before other people see them. Which service checks the images?

options.text: Amazon Rekognition content moderation
options.why: It labels unsafe or inappropriate content, so the app can hide an image or send it for a person to review.

options.text: Amazon Textract
options.why: Textract reads text and forms from documents. It doesn't judge images.

options.text: Amazon EFS
options.why: EFS stores files; it doesn't look at them.

steps.text: Find the same person in many photos
steps.question: A family photo app wants to find every picture of one person across thousands of photos. What does Rekognition offer?

options.text: Face search: index the faces into a collection, then search it with a photo
options.why: Rekognition compares faces against the collection you built, with a similarity score for each match.

options.text: It reads the names printed on everyone's clothes
options.why: That's not how face search works; it compares faces.

options.text: It turns each photo into a spreadsheet
options.why: Spreadsheets aren't involved. Rekognition returns faces, labels and scores.

quests.title: Tex Reads the Forms
quests.intro: Scanned pages, crooked tables, boxes filled in by hand: bring them to my scriptorium and I'll copy out what matters.

steps.text: Walk to the Textract Scriptorium and meet Tex
Learn 4 Textract cards about text, tables and forms
Save a clinic from retyping forms
steps.question: A clinic has thousands of scanned forms, and staff retype the name and date boxes by hand. What can Amazon Textract do?

options.text: Read the forms and return each field as a key and value, plus tables and text
options.why: Textract finds form fields, tables and lines of text, so an app can file them without retyping.

options.text: Translate the forms into other languages
options.why: Translation is Amazon Translate's job.

options.text: Store the scans cheaply
options.why: Storing files is a job for Amazon S3.

steps.text: Handle a messy handwritten box
steps.question: Textract isn't sure about one handwritten field. What should the app do?

options.text: Check the confidence score Textract returns, and send unsure fields to a person to review
options.why: Every result comes with a confidence score. Low scores are the ones a person should check.

options.text: Accept every answer as it comes
options.why: Unchecked mistakes end up in the clinic's records.

options.text: Throw the whole form away
options.why: One unclear box doesn't make the rest of the form wrong.
